GAP_A.name: OSIRIAN_BODY_PART_RELIC_GEOGRAPHY_TO_MENDES
why: Egyptian-source traditions independently place Osiris/Osiris-ba at Mendes across multiple periods.
Late Egyptian relic lists specifically assign phallus plus backbone to the Mendesian nome.
Papyrus Brooklyn independently gives the Mendesian Osiris a virile-member plus backbone divine-flesh identity.
Dendera traditions add rejuvenation/reassembly semantics at Mendes.
GAP_A.remaining_limit: This does not establish a continuous physical chain from the mythic original member to a surviving object.

GAP_B.name: MENDES_OSIRIAN_RELIC_TRADITION_TO_CG53469_AS_UNIQUE_ORIGINAL_MEMBER
GAP_B.forward_problem: No inspected ancient source predicts JE35425/CG53469 specifically, its 1902 burial, or its identity as the one original divine member.
GAP_B.reverse_problem: The object's secure available provenance points to a human funerary mummy of Nesbanebdjedet, not directly to an Osiris temple relic deposit.
GAP_B.matched_control_pressure: Comparable genital covers/models show that the object class is funerary/ritual and not uniquely divine.

GAP_C.name: EGYPTIAN_LANGUAGE_EXPLICIT_ORIGINAL_LOSS_EVENT
GAP_C.note: The continuous river/fish loss narrative remains most explicit in Plutarch in the current inspected chain; native Egyptian material strongly attests restoration, body-part identity, relic geography and Mendesian phallus functions but has not yet yielded the same complete loss narrative in this pass.
